source_refs.note: Topic 14.6 (PDF 31); Fig 14.9 is redrawn from the equations. The book's statement that acceleration and displacement differ in phase by pi/2 is corrected in a warning. The check question is added.

blocks.text: The displacement, velocity and acceleration of a body executing S.H.M. can be shown on graphs against time (Fig 14.9).

items: Displacement: x = xo cos(wt) (14.19). The particle has its maximum displacement xo at the extreme positions.

blocks.alt: Graph of displacement against time over one period, with dashed lines at each quarter period and at xo and -xo. The curve starts at +xo, falls through zero to -xo and rises back to +xo.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.9 (a): Graphical representation of displacement of oscillation performing S.H.M (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.9 (a)).

items: Velocity: its magnitude is xo w sin(wt) (14.20); taking direction into account, v = -xo w sin(wt). The speed is maximum, xo w, at the mean position and zero at the extreme positions.

blocks.alt: Graph of velocity against time over one period, between xo omega and -xo omega. The curve starts at zero, falls to -xo omega after a quarter period, crosses zero at half a period, reaches +xo omega at three quarters and returns to zero.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.9 (b): Graphical representation of velocity of oscillation performing S.H.M (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.9 (b)).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 14.9(b) shows the velocity rising first (v = +xo w sin wt). For x = xo cos wt the velocity is v = -xo w sin wt, so it falls first, as drawn above.

items: Acceleration: a = -w^2 x; putting x = xo cos(wt), a = -xo w^2 cos(wt) (14.21). The acceleration is maximum, xo w^2, at the extreme positions and zero at the mean position.

blocks.alt: Graph of acceleration against time over one period, between omega squared xo and minus omega squared xo. The curve starts at its most negative value, rises through zero to its maximum at half a period and falls back: always opposite to the displacement.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.9 (c): Graphical representation of acceleration of oscillation performing S.H.M (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.9 (c)).

blocks.text: From the graphs: the phase difference between velocity and displacement is pi/2, and the phase difference between acceleration and displacement is pi.
